protections: Outbound HTTP(S) requests made on behalf of a user-supplied URL must be restricted to allowed targets: only http/https, and no host that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata address, with the decision enforced at connect time so a second name resolution or a redirect target cannot change it.
The control-panel resource-js proxy must fetch only URLs belonging to the control panel's own resource origin, and that reference origin must not be derivable from request data the caller supplies.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Asset mutations are gated by an explicitly granted GraphQL schema action (volumes.<uid>.create / save), so the caller is treated as a trusted API consumer.
The action already rejects URLs that do not start with the control-panel resource base URL and requires a control-panel request, so it looks origin-locked.
config/guzzle.php is site-owned, so a value merged over the default client configuration is not something an attacker supplies.
Once the URL's hostname has been resolved and the address checked at the call site, the request is assumed to go to that same checked address.
Redirects are normal HTTP behaviour, and the URL that was supplied and validated is assumed to be the URL that is fetched.
The dev-server probe is dev-only tooling that must be able to reach a loopback dev server; it is not attacker-controlled, so it must keep working rather than be blocked.

masking: T5 (a second name resolution at connect time) only becomes the remaining path once a target-address check exists; in the pinned tree the metadata address is reachable directly at src/gql/resolvers/mutations/Asset.php:258.
T6 (a redirect target that was never validated) likewise only matters once the initial URL is checked at src/gql/resolvers/mutations/Asset.php:258.

conflicts.what: The one-line fix for T1/T5 - blocking private and loopback targets in the shared Guzzle client - makes the webpack dev-server probe at src/services/Webpack.php:216-218 (http://localhost:8082 or host.docker.internal) fail, silently disabling dev-server asset URLs.

Connect-time address pinning cannot be enforced through the configured httpProxy that src/Craft.php:397-399 forces onto every client, so a fix that pins the target address breaks sites using a proxy and a fix that honours the proxy leaves the rebind case open.

fairness_risks: A rule that refuses loopback/private targets contradicts the legitimate dev-server loopback fetch (src/services/Webpack.php:216-218) and local/Craftnet-mock base API URLs (src/base/ApplicationTrait.php:235).

A rule that refuses redirects contradicts legitimate asset URLs that redirect (http-to-https, CDN/signed URLs); the pinned client sets no redirect policy at src/Craft.php:383-387, so the default behaviour is kept.
A blanket address guard inside the public Craft::createGuzzleClient() (src/Craft.php:380) also applies to plugin code that intentionally calls an internal service through that documented helper.

The T2 fix must keep working for installs that legitimately serve the control panel from an aliased/dynamic @web base URL (src/config/GeneralConfig.php:2473 plus src/web/Request.php:219), so simply freezing the reference origin can break valid deployments.

design.why: Each trap has a different reason to dismiss and a different site: T1 is the route the metadata report names, dismissed as 'requires a GraphQL schema action' (src/gql/resolvers/mutations/Asset.php:77); T2 is an unmentioned anonymous route whose origin reference is itself caller-supplied, dismissed as 'already same-origin and control-panel only' (src/controllers/AppController.php:113); T5 is the shape a correct-looking T1 fix still fails, because the address is checked once while the connection resolves again, dismissed as 'I resolved and checked the IP'; T7 is the coupled value that punishes over-hardening the shared client, dismissed as 'dev-only loopback'. T1 sits in the GraphQL resolver, T2 in the controller, T5 in the connect-time path of Craft::createGuzzleClient, and T7 in the dev-server probe, so fixing one does not close the others, and T6 rides along with T5 as the unvalidated redirect hop. It beats a single shared-client guard because that guard would break T7 and cannot be enforced through the httpProxy at src/Craft.php:397-399.

unverified: Fix commit 013db636fdb3 (advisory A) is not visible in the pinned tree: no host/address validation exists anywhere under src and the last 'Fixed an SSRF vulnerability' entry is CHANGELOG.md:1940 (4.4.2), so 'does A leave B open' and 'is B in code A wrote' cannot be read from the pinned code.
Which route advisory A actually names is unknown (the record's summary describes B, DNS rebinding); T1 is assumed to be the metadata SSRF surface and T2 the uncovered route.

Yii aliases AssetManager::$baseUrl ('@web/cpresources' from src/config/GeneralConfig.php:2473 into an absolute URL) and @web is built from HTTP_HOST at src/web/Request.php:219; the aliasing step is framework behaviour not visible in the pinned tree, and it is what makes the T2 reference value caller-supplied.

Guzzle's defaults (follow redirects, resolve names again at connect time) are library behaviour, not visible in the pinned tree; the pinned client simply sets no handler or redirect policy (src/Craft.php:383-401).

If the reference fix is one address-validation handler inside Craft::createGuzzleClient(), then T1 and T2 would be closed by the same fix site as T4/T5/T6 and the four groups above collapse into one; the pinned tree does not show where A's fix landed.
Whether curl normalises dot-segments in the request path (part of T2's lexical prefix weakness) is library behaviour and was not verified here.

The exact reachability of the resource-js action depends on the control-panel request detection at src/web/Request.php:229-288 and on whether the install uses the default '@web/cpresources' alias rather than an absolute resourceBaseUrl.
